questions.q: Given function formatAmount(value: string | number) { return value.toFixed(2); }, why does this fail to compile?
options: toFixed doesn't exist in TypeScript at all
toFixed exists on number but not on string, and TypeScript can't be sure which type value is at that point
Union types cannot have any methods called on them ever
toFixed requires two arguments
questions.explain: Since value could be either a string or a number, TypeScript refuses to let you call a number-only method until it's proven which type value actually is.

questions.q: What does wrapping the toFixed call in if (typeof value === "number") { ... } accomplish?
options: It converts value to a number at runtime
It narrows value to specifically number inside that block, so TypeScript allows calling toFixed there
It has no effect on the type checker, only on runtime behavior
It removes the need for the union type entirely
questions.explain: TypeScript recognizes the typeof check and narrows value's type to number for the rest of that block, allowing number-only methods to be called safely.

questions.q: Why is Array.isArray(input) used instead of typeof input === "array" to check for an array?
options: typeof "array" is valid but slower
typeof on an array returns "object", not "array", so Array.isArray is the correct way to detect one
Arrays don't have a runtime type at all
Both approaches are equally invalid
questions.explain: JavaScript's typeof operator returns "object" for arrays, so Array.isArray() is the dedicated check needed to narrow an array type specifically.

questions.q: In a discriminated union like { status: "confirmed"; blockNumber: number } | { status: "failed"; reason: string }, what does checking result.status === "confirmed" do?
options: It only narrows the status field itself, leaving the rest of the object type unchanged
It narrows the entire object, so TypeScript knows blockNumber exists in that branch and reason does not
It throws a runtime error if status is anything else
It has no effect since status is just a string
questions.explain: Checking a shared literal 'discriminant' field narrows the whole union down to the matching variant, making the rest of that variant's properties (like blockNumber) safely accessible.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four narrowing tools highlighted in this lesson?
options: typeof for primitives
instanceof for class instances
Array.isArray for arrays
parseInt for converting strings to numbers
questions.explain: parseInt converts a string to a number at runtime, but it isn't a type-narrowing mechanism — the four narrowing tools covered are typeof, instanceof, Array.isArray, and discriminated unions.
